name: JEE Main
short_description: An entrance exam used in engineering admission routes at participating institutions.
difficulty_note: NTA reported 1,538,468 unique candidates appeared for JEE Main Paper 1 across the 2026 sessions. This is exam volume, not an admission probability for a particular course.
prep_note: Start with the current NTA syllabus and identify topic gaps in mathematics, physics, and chemistry; use timed sets and review errors before adding more mocks. Check official cutoffs and eligibility, build a balanced institution list, and compare engineering routes that do not depend on one rank.

name: NEET (UG)
short_description: A common entrance test used for admission to undergraduate medical courses in India.
difficulty_note: NTA listed approximately 22.79 lakh registrations for the scheduled May 3, 2026 sitting. That scale is not an admission rate; eligibility, seats, and cutoffs vary by course, state, and institution.
prep_note: Begin with the latest NTA bulletin and syllabus, then plan biology, chemistry, and physics study around your topic gaps and timed practice. Check current result, re-exam, counselling, eligibility, and seat notices for your target course and state; compare other health and life-science routes too.
example_status: Starter example — fact-check and expand before treating this as final guidance.

name: CUET (UG)
short_description: Scores are used for undergraduate admission by participating universities across India.
difficulty_note: NTA counted 1,568,867 unique registrations across 37 subjects for CUET (UG) 2026. Course-level competition and selection rules vary by university and programme.
prep_note: List target courses first, then map each university's official subject combination, eligibility, and selection rules. Practice only the relevant sections and use the current CUET bulletin; add alternate programmes or universities because one score does not determine every route.

name: CLAT (UG)
short_description: A national admission test for undergraduate law programmes at participating National Law Universities.
difficulty_note: The Consortium reported 75,009 candidates registered for CLAT UG 2026. That count is not an admission rate; outcomes vary by rank, category, NLU, and available seats.
prep_note: Use the current Consortium paper pattern to plan reading comprehension, reasoning, legal awareness, current-affairs review, and timed practice. Check seat and admission notices, and include other law programmes in your list rather than relying on one route.

name: Common Admission Test (CAT)
short_description: A management admission test used by the Indian Institutes of Management and other participating institutions.
difficulty_note: Highly competitive for many sought-after programmes; CAT is one input, and each school sets its own shortlist and admission criteria.
prep_note: Build quantitative practice, verbal and reading work, and data interpretation and reasoning into a schedule, then use timed mocks to identify specific gaps. Check each school's current selection policy because academic history, work experience, interviews, or other factors may also matter; keep other management programmes or exams on your list.

name: SAT
short_description: A college admission test that some U.S. colleges use as part of their application review.
difficulty_note: Use and score expectations differ by college; some schools have test-optional policies.
prep_note: College testing policies and score expectations differ and can change, so check each college's current policy before registering. If the SAT is relevant, use official practice to find sections to work on and compare any published score ranges as context, not a promise; consider test-optional application routes where available.

prep_note: College testing policies and score expectations differ and can change, so check each college's current policy before registering. name: A-levels
short_description: A subject-based qualification route often used in higher-education applications; it is not a single competitive entrance exam.
difficulty_note: Assessment depends on the subjects and awarding body; course offers set their own requirements.
prep_note: A-levels are a subject qualification, not a single entrance exam. Choose subjects after checking prerequisites for several courses you may apply to, and ask a teacher or adviser how the awarding body's assessment works; requirements can differ across courses and UK nations.

name: UCAT
short_description: An admissions test used by participating UK and partner universities for some medicine and dentistry courses.
difficulty_note: Competitive admissions component; requirements and selection methods vary by university and course.
prep_note: First confirm whether your target medicine or dentistry courses require the UCAT in the current cycle. If they do, learn the current format and use the Consortium's official practice materials under timed conditions; check each course's other selection stages and keep related health or science routes in view.
